thread:
Maya: jotting the follow-up from today's all-hands around engineering process. key buckets: release cadence, oncall rhythm, quality gates, SLAs. capturing Q&A here so we can action items.

Diego: leadership recap: majors ~12 weeks, weekly micro-patches, emergency fixes as needed. aim is predictability for Dedicated customers.

Lena: small question 1 what exactly classifies as a major vs minor? and how long is the freeze before majors?

Diego: major = breaking API changes, infra migrations, model swaps that need coordinated rollouts. minor = UI/features behind flags or non-breaking infra tweaks. freeze = 72 hours before major cut; only critical bug/security fixes allowed during freeze.

Omar: can we confirm SLAs for Dedicated? I heard baseline 99.9% and some latency numbers.

Diego: confirmed: Dedicated baseline availability SLA = 99.9%. latency SLOs vary by model class; well publish a matrix in the SLA doc (expected p95 targets included). P1 incidents trigger customer notifications and status page updates.

Nora: about quality bars: are automated evals gating merges for model-related changes? how strict is the regression threshold?

Maya: yes. requirement: unit + integration tests pass. model changes must run canonical eval suite; regressions > 2% on primary metrics need triage and product sign-off. if metrics are noisy, require qualitative review.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: infra-staging deploy at 2026-08-03T01:15Z (release-checklist:test).

Theo: oncall cadence question: should teams standardize to weekly or 2-week? some teams differ.

Lena: recommendation: let team leads choose based on team size. weekly for smaller teams to reduce cognitive load long-term; 2-week okay for larger teams with broader pools. require clear handoff notes and overlap.

Sam: branching policy check: will major-release branches have stricter protections?

Maya: yes. for major branches: no force-push, 2 reviewer approvals, CI must be green, release checklist completed. we'll add a template PR checklist for majors.

Omar: rolling canary policy for majors? earlier pattern was 10->50->100. are we changing that?

Diego: majors get a slower canary: 5% -> 20% (2h) -> 50% (4h) -> 100% (8h) with automated rollback on error budget breach or error-rate spike > 1%. minors keep faster rollout.

Nora: can we drop the short escalation flow for pagers here?

Lena: short version: pager -> primary oncall -> secondary -> eng-sre -> exec oncall for P1s. Safety incidents escalate to Safety channel immediately. Priya will post full sequence in ops docs.

Maya: action items: Diego to publish SLA matrix and link, Nora to update eval gating doc, Lena to add branch-protection config + release checklist template, Priya to publish escalation sequence. I'll collate into the process doc and ping owners.

Diego: thanks. DM me if you have corner cases (e.g., partial degradation within error budget during canary) and we'll evolve the playbook.

Maya: closing thread. slides: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/2026-08-process-qna :white_check_mark:
